subject.title: Prompt-cache prefix churn on OpenAI models: per-turn dynamic injections (message tool hint + volatile system-prompt section) defeat automatic prefix caching

question: Should repair wait for live current-main OpenAI/Codex cache telemetry, or is the source-proven `message_tool_only` schema churn enough to authorize a scoped fix now?
rationale: Source inspection proves the reported tool-schema byte drift remains, but the exact current-main provider cache-hit impact was not live-tested and the fix can affect visible reply delivery semantics.

options.title: Require live proof first
options.body: Keep the issue open for maintainer review and gather a current-main OpenAI/Codex run showing `cacheRead` drops tied to `message_tool_only` before authorizing repair.

options.title: Authorize source-backed repair
options.body: Treat the remaining schema churn as sufficient proof and queue a narrow fix that moves the per-turn directive into late turn content with delivery regression tests.

options.title: Deprioritize as optimization
options.body: Leave the issue open as a lower-priority cost/performance item until broader prompt-cache work is scheduled.

recommendation.title: Require live proof first
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open for maintainer review and gather a current-main OpenAI/Codex run showing `cacheRead` drops tied to `message_tool_only` before authorizing repair.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main touches and adjacent prompt-cache stabilization work make this the strongest available routing candidate.
